subject: Post-call recap & qualification: ClearWave embedding pilot — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gold <sara@clearwave.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & qualification: ClearWave embedding pilot — next steps

Thanks for the time today, Sara and Tom — appreciate the clear context on ClearWave's search latency targets and the evaluation metrics you care about. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum:

• Primary goal: improve semantic search recall for tag+synonym queries and reduce false positives on short queries (<6 tokens).
• Key constraints: max median latency 45ms per query at 20 qps, retention of metadata for 18 months, SOC2 evidence required for pilot.
• Data scope for pilot: 1.2M document index (product docs + support threads), subset of ~50k high-value documents for initial embed benchmarking.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood sends recommended embedding models and a small benchmark package (prompt sets + evaluation harness) — target delivery Wed 5/6 EOD.
2) ClearWave shares access to a 50k sample and the canonical query set (we discussed query categories) — target by Fri 5/8.
3) Align on pilot success metrics (semantic MAP@10, median latency at target QPS, dimensionality/storage estimate) — agree by next call.

Attachments: I attached a quick benchmark CSV template and a draft pilot MOP (more details in the Drive link).

If that all looks right I'll kick off bench runs with Rishi and loop Marissa for the productionization checklist (rollout options + infra sizing).

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Gold <sara@clearwave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@clearwave.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 19:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & qualification: ClearWave embedding pilot — next steps

Thanks Ben — that matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from my side:

• Query set: we'll provide 3 categories — product lookup (phrase-heavy), support intent (short), and exploratory (longer). The short/support ones are highest priority.
• SOC2: we can share the audit contact, but ClearWave's procurement will need a SOC2 letter and a dataflow diagram before signing the pilot MSA.

We can get the 50k sample ready by Friday. Please include a recommended model list and a short paragraph on how you evaluate dimensionality vs storage tradeoffs — Tom is sensitive to index size for our US region infra.

Sara
Sara Gold | Head of Search, ClearWave Analytics
Sara@clearwave.ai | +1 (212) 555-3410

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gold <sara@clearwave.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@clearwave.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & qualification: ClearWave embedding pilot — next steps

Sara / Tom — following up with the model and eval artifacts we discussed. High-level recommendations (short list to keep the pilot focused):

1) Recommended models (initial):
  - SBERT-large-enc (384d) — strong baseline for short queries, lower false positives on exact-match synonyms.
  - RW-embed-quant-2 (256d, int8) — good cost/latency tradeoff; recommended for tight storage budgets.
  - Sentence-Turbo-1024 (1024d) — for long-form exploratory queries where semantic nuance matters; use as optional comparator.

2) Evaluation package included:
  - prompt_sets/ : curated query lists (support_short.csv, product_phrase.csv, exploratory_long.csv)
  - bench_runner/README.md : how to run local bench harness (Docker + sample scoring script)
  - perf_targets.md : latency scoring rubric at 5/20/50 qps

3) Dimensionality notes:
  - 384d SBERT gives ~2.2x smaller index vs 1024d for the same corpus; 256d quantized can reduce storage by ~40% vs fp16 384d but watch recall loss on long/contextual queries.
  - We'll include a quick storage estimate in the CSV (attached).

Attached: clearwave-benchmark-results.csv (template with placeholders), pilot-mop-draft.docx (scope/MOP). Also linking the eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ClearWavePilot

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@clearwave.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Gold <sara@clearwave.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & qualification: ClearWave embedding pilot — next steps

Appreciate the package, Rishi — looks actionable. A few quick points from our infra team: 

• Please include a worst-case index size (GB) for 1.2M docs for each model recommendation; we'll need that for capacity planning.
• For quantized options, can you indicate expected median latency at 20 qps on an m60-equivalent instance? That helps our ops team compare cost.
• Proc wants an estimate of how long the pilot MSA review will take — we typically need 7–10 business days once SOC2 docs are provided.

We'll upload the 50k sample by EOD Friday to the shared folder. If you can return a short internal note with the storage/latency estimates and a recommended one-model starting point (low-risk) by Monday morning, we can get procurement moving.

—Tom
Tom Nguyen | Infrastructure Lead, ClearWave Analytics
procurement@clearwave.ai
